learner_words: Marlo said this one felt like a race in her brain too and she liked going fast. She said sometimes the sounds "get in the wrong seats" which I thought was adorable and also incredibly accurate.
guide_note: Wednesday session! Word Chain Race was a hit in terms of engagement — Marlo loves anything with a timer or a competitive feel, which is very on-brand for her. 11 out of 14 is honestly a solid result. The reversals in short blends are something we've been tracking for a while now. Her educational psychologist flagged this in last year's dyslexia assessment as a sequencing difficulty that often co-occurs with the kind of processing profile Marlo has. It's not just carelessness — she's working SO hard. The ADHD piece also means that once she gets into a rhythm she sometimes rushes and the sequencing errors go up. I mentioned the reversal pattern in a comment on a post by @dyslexia_homeschool_collective which has been a fantastic community for us. I also found a really useful article at https://learningdifferencesdaily.com/blend-reversal-interventions that I'm going to try adapting for our Friday session. Going to email Marlo's reading specialist at dr.fontaine.reads@childliteracyclinic.ca with this week's notes so she has them before our November check-in.
